newsitem.title: ISRAEL: No charges against Netanyahu - Israel Radio.
newsitem.headline: No charges against Netanyahu - Israel Radio.

text.p: Israel Radio said on Sunday prosecutors had decided not to charge Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a corruption scandal but to indict a key coalition ally.

"The prosecutors' report recommends filing only one indictment, against legislator Aryeh Deri on charges of obstructing justice in connection with his current trial," the radio's political correspondent said. "The report recommends not to submit charges against the prime minister and Justice Minister Tzachi Hanegbi."

The radio report came minutes after prosecutors distributed copies of their decision to Netanyahu and the three other officials who police had recommended be charged in connection with the short-lived appointment of an attorney general.

The radio said the report had recommended continuing an investigation of Avigdor Lieberman, director-general of the prime minister's office, and two others not previously mentioned in the scandal, a top lawyer and a prominent Likud activist.

Israeli media reports had speculated Netanyahu would not be charged but said the findings could be critical of his handling of the appointment in January of Likud political crony Roni Bar-On as attorney general.
The radio report came 35 minutes before the scheduled start of a Justice Ministry news conference to announce the prosecutors' findings.
